correctness.rationale: The source-specified positive weights are summable by a geometric envelope. Direct adjacent log-mass ratios prove strict log-concavity and every exact modal cutoff. The two-rate log-likelihood increment equals -alpha(b-a)+(alpha+1)[F(n+1)-F(n)]. The exact sign of F'' changes once because cosh(bx/2)/cosh(ax/2) increases strictly, forcing all positive forward differences of F to decrease and yielding a single crossing of every positive threshold. The first increment thus determines the necessary-and-sufficient all-index MLR condition. Integral averaging of (1+exp(t))^-1 establishes the strictly decreasing critical-shape curve and unique second-rate root. A normalization-free rational witness confirms actual failure on one side. A standalone script was executed and passed; finite checks are supporting evidence, not the proof.

value.rationale: The very source of the density-sampled generalized half-logistic count law identifies its added shape as a remedy for fixed-mode-zero modeling limitations but leaves the generalization largely unexplored. The exact criterion pinpoints when comparing count samples at different rates supports the strong monotone likelihood-ratio order used in one-sided testing and monotone comparisons, and when it demonstrably fails despite strict log-concavity of each distribution. The unexpected re-entry into the LR-ordered regime after a uniquely determined larger rate makes a natural full classification rather than a numerical improvement or a routine single coefficient check. The exact modal staircase and boundary ties directly support fitting count data with nonzero modes. No specific application has been empirically validated here; the value is mathematical and methodological.
risks: Practical effect sizes and inferential power are not assessed.
